guitar.guitaristsText: Eric Clapton / Jeff Beck / Jimmy Page (successive lead guitarists)
guitar.modelsText: Fender Esquire/Telecaster (Page era) / Gibson ES-335 / Fender Strat (Beck era)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: The Yardbirds famously had three legendary guitarists pass through in succession (Clapton, Beck, Page), each with documented gear, though no single instrument represents the whole band.
guitar.notes: Notable band for having three iconic guitarists; gear varies by era.

tone.target: fuzzy 60s psychedelic lead with sharp sustain

tone.summary: A fuzzy, mid-focused signal chain using a Fuzz distortion, followed by a classic UK amp model (UK 45) to capture the raw, psychedelic 60s sound with sharp sustain.

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise from the fuzz and vintage amp simulation.
Provide the required fuzzy bite and psychedelic texture for a 60s sound.
Slightly boost the signal into the amp to ensure maximum sustain and presence.
blocks.gap: Using Boost for general level lift, as a dedicated EQ pre-boost is not strictly necessary here.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the British combo amp sound and provide the necessary mid-focus for 60s rock.
Provide the classic British cabinet tone that pairs well with the UK 45 amp model.
Enhance the upper mids and overall bite required for psychedelic lead work.
Optional subtle modulation to add depth without sounding too 'lush' (kept low for 60s feel).
blocks.gap: The verdict advises against lush modulation, so this is kept minimal and optional.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and dimension without sounding overly modern or wet.
Used sparingly for rhythmic echo on leads, but kept off by default to maintain raw 60s feel.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the raw, mid-focused sound of a vintage British combo.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw, mid-focused bite needed for 60s psychedelic leads.
